profile.name: Vivian Adjeikaa Doe
profile.tagline:
I am beginning to see myself as a scholar interested in rhetoric and feminist thought. I am particularly interested in questions of voice, representation, agency, and power:
who gets to speak,who gets represented,
who controls that representation,and whose knowledge is recognized.
I am a theatre artist, media and communication researcher and writing instructor
profile.status: Open to research and teaching collaboration
profile.bio:
I am a Ph.D. student in Rhetoric, Theory and Culture at North Dakota State University, where I also teach First Year College Composition as a Graduate Teaching Assistant.

My path into scholarship began on the stage. I trained in theatre at the University of Education, Winneba, and earned a Master of Fine Arts in Drama and Film Studies in the Department of Directing at The Central Academy of Drama in Beijing. Along the way I have taught drama, communication skills and African studies in Ghana and China, directed student productions, and led the Ghana Embassy cultural troupe in China.

My research, published with the School of Media and Communication at Shanghai Jiao Tong University, asks how ordinary people find and use a public voice: how community theatre turns audiences into active citizens in Ghana, how social media shapes democracy and freedom of expression, how women journalists navigate newsroom patriarchy, and how online communities share health information. At NDSU I am extending this work to rhetoric and African digital activism. I am a member of the Coalition of Feminist Scholars in the History of Rhetoric and Composition.
profile.interests: Rhetoric on Voice and Trauma, Community and applied theatre, digital activism,  Online behaviour, Drama education, First-year writing
